instruction: Write a function that flattens a nested list of integers into a single flat list, preserving order.
pivot_note: Fork is at function body start; recursive uses self-calls, iterative uses a stack/deque.
docstring: Return a flat list of all integers from the nested input list, preserving order.

instruction: Write a function that returns the sum of all integers in a nested list of arbitrary depth.
pivot_note: Fork is at function body start; both strategies are well-represented in training data.
docstring: Return the sum of all integers in a nested list (arbitrary depth).

instruction: Write a function that returns the maximum nesting depth of a nested list. A flat non-empty list has depth 1; the empty list has depth 0.
pivot_note: Fork is at function body start; recursive version returns 1 + max(max_depth) over sublists.
docstring: Return the maximum nesting depth. A flat non-empty list has depth 1; an empty list has depth 0.

instruction: Write a function that returns the product of all integers in a flat list. Return 1 for an empty list.
pivot_note: Fork is at body start; recursive uses head * product_list(tail), iterative uses a running product.
docstring: Return the product of all integers in lst. Return 1 for an empty list.

instruction: Write a function that returns the sum of the decimal digits of a non-negative integer.
pivot_note: Fork is at body start; recursive: n%10 + sum_digits(n//10), iterative: while n > 0 loop.
docstring: Return the sum of the decimal digits of non-negative integer n.

instruction: Write a function that computes the digital root of a non-negative integer: repeatedly sum its digits until a single-digit number remains.
pivot_note: Fork is at body start; recursive calls sum_digits (possibly inlined), iterative uses while n >= 10 loop.
docstring: Repeatedly sum the digits of n until a single digit is obtained; return that digit. n >= 0.

instruction: Write a function that removes consecutive duplicate elements from a list, preserving order.
pivot_note: Fork is at body start; iterative tracks previous element, recursive compares head to first element of tail.
docstring: Return a new list with consecutive duplicate elements removed, preserving order.

instruction: Write a function that returns a new list with the elements in reverse order, without using slicing or built-in reverse.
pivot_note: Fork is at body start; docstring rules out the trivial one-liner to force a real strategy choice.
docstring: Return a new list with elements of lst in reverse order (without slicing or reversed()).

instruction: Write a function that returns True if a list reads the same forwards and backwards.
pivot_note: Fork is at body start; recursive: compare first/last and recurse on middle, iterative: two-pointer loop.
docstring: Return True if lst reads the same forwards and backwards.

instruction: Write a function that counts the total number of non-list (leaf) elements in a nested list.
pivot_note: Fork is at body start; structurally identical to sum_nested but counts instead of sums.
docstring: Return the total number of non-list elements (leaves) in a nested list of arbitrary depth.

instruction: Write a function that returns the nth Fibonacci number (0-indexed: fib(0)=0, fib(1)=1).
pivot_note: Classic fork; both versions are textbook examples. Memoised recursive and iterative with two variables are both common.
docstring: Return the nth Fibonacci number (0-indexed: fib(0)=0, fib(1)=1, fib(2)=1, ...).

instruction: Write a function that returns the nth triangle number: 1 + 2 + ... + n. Return 0 for n=0.
pivot_note: Fork at body start; recursive: n + triangle_number(n-1), iterative: accumulate over range(1, n+1).
docstring: Return the nth triangle number (1 + 2 + ... + n). Return 0 when n is 0.

instruction: Write a function that returns 1^2 + 2^2 + ... + n^2. Return 0 for n=0.
pivot_note: Fork at body start; recursive: n*n + sum_squares(n-1), iterative: accumulate over range(1, n+1).
docstring: Return 1^2 + 2^2 + ... + n^2 for n >= 0. Return 0 when n is 0.

instruction: Write a function that counts the number of even integers in a flat list.
pivot_note: Fork at body start; recursive: (lst[0]%2==0) + count_even(lst[1:]), iterative: for loop with counter.
docstring: Return the count of even integers in the flat list lst.

instruction: Write a function that removes all falsy values from a flat list, preserving order. Treat 0 and null/None as falsy.
pivot_note: Fork at body start; recursive: filter head then recurse, iterative: for loop accumulating truthy elements.
docstring: Return a new list with all falsy values (None/nullopt, 0) removed.

instruction: Write a function that inserts a null/None sentinel between every two adjacent elements of a list. A list of 0 or 1 elements is returned unchanged.
pivot_note: Fork at body start; recursive: [lst[0], None] + interleave_none(lst[1:]), iterative: loop with append pairs.
docstring: Return a new list with a null sentinel inserted between every two adjacent elements: [1,2,3] -> [1,null,2,null,3].

instruction: Write a function that computes the alternating sum of a list: a[0] - a[1] + a[2] - a[3] + ...
pivot_note: Fork at body start; recursive: lst[0] - alternating_sum(lst[1:]), iterative: enumerate with sign flip.
docstring: Return a[0] - a[1] + a[2] - ... (alternating signs starting with +). Return 0 for empty list.

instruction: Write a function that returns a new list where every element of the input appears twice consecutively.
pivot_note: Fork at body start; recursive: [lst[0], lst[0]] + duplicate_each(lst[1:]), iterative: for loop appending pairs.
docstring: Return a new list where each element of lst appears twice: [1,2,3] -> [1,1,2,2,3,3].

instruction: Write a function that returns a list of running maximums: each element is the maximum of all elements up to and including that position.
pivot_note: Fork at body start; iterative (track current max) is most natural, but recursive version is also valid.
docstring: Return a list where element i is max(lst[0], ..., lst[i]).

instruction: Write a function that returns a list of sums of adjacent pairs: [a, b, c, d] -> [a+b, b+c, c+d].
pivot_note: Fork at body start; iterative (for i in range) is natural, recursive (lst[0]+lst[1] then recurse on tail) also valid.
docstring: Return [lst[i]+lst[i+1] for i in range(len(lst)-1)], or [] if len(lst) < 2.

instruction: Write a function that returns the factorial of a non-negative integer n (0! = 1).
pivot_note: Fork at function body start; recursive: return n * factorial(n-1), iterative: for loop with accumulator.
docstring: Return the factorial of non-negative integer n (0! = 1).

instruction: Write a function that returns the number of 1-bits in the binary representation of a non-negative integer n.
pivot_note: Fork at body start; recursive: (n&1) + count_set_bits(n>>1), iterative: while n > 0 with n &= n-1 or n >>= 1.
docstring: Return the number of 1-bits in the binary representation of non-negative integer n.

instruction: Write a function that returns the integer formed by reversing the decimal digits of n (n >= 0). E.g. 1234 -> 4321.
pivot_note: Fork at body start; iterative: while n > 0 with digit extraction, recursive less common but valid.
docstring: Return the integer formed by reversing the decimal digits of n (n >= 0). E.g. 1234 -> 4321.

instruction: Write a function that returns the number of steps to reach 1 in the Collatz sequence starting from n > 0. If n is even: next = n/2. If n is odd: next = 3*n+1.
pivot_note: Fork at body start; recursive: 1 + collatz_steps(next), iterative: while n != 1 loop.
docstring: Return the number of steps to reach 1 in the Collatz sequence starting from n > 0.

instruction: Write a function that returns the greatest common divisor of two non-negative integers a and b.
pivot_note: Euclid's algorithm; recursive (return gcd(b, a%b)) and iterative (while b) are both textbook.
docstring: Return the greatest common divisor of non-negative integers a and b.
